Kabc020131362022
 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
 Court Of Small Causes, At Bengaluru. (Scch-25) 
 - : Present:- 
 Smt. Prakriti Kalyanpur, B.A(L),Ll.B., Ll.M.
 Xxiii Additional Small Causes Judge, Bengaluru.
 Dated This The 28Th Day Of August 2024 
 Mvc No.2141/2022 
 PETITIONER: Mr. Rajesh K.N.
 S/o. Nagaraja Gupta,
 Aged about 50 years,
 R/at No.1006,
 Vasavi Temple Road,
 21st Ward, Magadi,
 Magadi Taluk,
 Ramanagara District,
 Karnataka - 562 120. 
 (By Sri. N.Shivaram,
 Advocate/s.)
 V/S  RESPONDENTS: 1. Mr. Ganesh C.K.
 S/o C.D.Kempanna,
 Aged about ...Major,
 R/at No.152,
 Cholanayakanahalli,
 Tippagondanahalli Post,
 Bangalore,
 Karnataka - 562 130.
 (RC owner of the Canter  bearing NO.KA-02-AF-5715)
 SCCH - 25 2 MVC 2141/2022  (By Sri. B.N.
 Gopala Krishna, Advocate.)
 2. The Regional Manager  United India Gen. Ins. Co.
 Ltd.,
 Regional Office, Motor TP,
 Hub, Krishi Bhavana,
 5th and 6th Floor,

 JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 28.08.2021.
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 07.02.2022 at about 2.30pm, the petitioner was proceeding as rider in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- JH-8063 on Bangalore - Magadi Road, in careful manner and when he reached near Reenac Factory Bangalore - Magadi Road,
Tavarekere Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk, Bangalore , a Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-5715 came from Bangalore to Magadi with high speed driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle. Due to the terrible impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Magadi Main Road, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for some days. So far he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards surgery and medical expenses,
nourishment and transportation expenses. 
4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy,
doing Tailoring and also working as Photographer and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot attend his work permanently, resulting in loss of earning and he is put to great financial hardship and untold misery. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-5715. The Tavarekere police have filed charge sheet against the driver in Cr.No.0042/2022 punishable u/Sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC. The 1 st Respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, this petition. 
5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements. 
6. The objections of the Respondent No.1:
Rajesh K.N vs Ganesh C.K on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125336287/
2 He has denied the averments of the petition and admitted that the vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AF-5715 was covered under insurance policy with 2nd respondent vide policy No.0723013120P2250P114457260 valid from 13.03.2021 to 12.03.2022 and the rider of the said Canter vehicle also possessed valid DL as on the date of accident.
He has denied the manner of accident, age, occupation, earning and medical expenses of the petitioner. Thereby he prayed for dismissal of the petition. 
7. The objections of the Respondent No.2: 
It has denied the averments made in the petition. The Issuance of policy and its validity was not confirmed. It has contended that If policy is issued and valid on the date of accident its liability is as per the terms and conditions of the said policy and provisions of MV Act. Further, the Respondent insurer has denied the manner of accident, petitioner's age, occupation, medical expenses, income and other details of the Petitioner. Therefore, it has sought for dismissal of the petition. 
8. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-5715 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries? 
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum? 
From whom payable? 
3. What order or award? 
9. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has got examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked Exs.P.1 to P.18. Dr.Arjun S. Prakash got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.19 to 21. On the other side, the Respondent No.2 has got examined Mr. P.Ramesh - Administration Officer as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2.
10. Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties. 
11. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  12. Issue No.1:
Rajesh K.N vs Ganesh C.K on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125336287/
3 In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-5715 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 8. PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination. The Respondent No.2 has denied the manner of accident and also denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle. In the cross-examination of PW.1, he has stated that he was going in the speed of 30 to 40km/hr. The accident was head on collision. There was repair work going on and the accident spot was also getting repaired. The accident occurred on the mud road not on the Tar Road which was connecting to other two pieces of Tar Road. The accident took place 5ft away from the left side of the Road. There was a ditch on the left side of the Road. 
13. The FIR at Ex.P.1 was registered on 07.02.2022 on the complaint of petitioner's wife at Ex.P.2. 
Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar shows the details and spot of the accident conducted on 08.02.2022 at 10.00am to 10.45am. Exs. P.4 & 5 are the notice issued to the Owner of the offending vehicle and reply to the said notice which reveals the details of the owner of the offending vehicle. Ex . P.7 MVA report shows that petitioner's vehicle damaged to its front right side indicator and front right side bumper scratched and the offending vehicle also damaged to its front wheel fender, front forks bent,
front shape of the body, front both side shapes, both side rear view mirrors, rear right side body,
rear silencer bent and front both side safety guard damaged. Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending Canter Lorry after thorough investigation. The respondent No.2 did not produce any document nor examined any witness in support of their contention to prove the negligence of the petitioner. Therefore, on the basis of doucments on record, the Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Canter bearing No.KA-02-AF-5715. Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative. 
14. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6. As per Ex.P.6, the Petitioner has sustained (i) Type III B Open fracture tibia with communition, (ii) Fracture lateral condyle (R) tibia,
(iii) Fracture clavicle (R), (iv) Laceration scalp of posterior,
(v) For laceration of forehead scalp and (vi) fracture of nasal bone. Out of these injuries, injury Nos.1, 2, 3, and 6 are grievous and injury Nos.4 & 5 are simple in nature. 
15. The Petitioner got examined Dr. Arjun S. Prakash as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.19 to 21 case sheet, old X- rays 8 in Nos., and X-rays 1 in Nos. He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and has stated the permanent physical disability of limbs due to fractures at 61.42%
and total permanent physical disability for whole body to fractures at 20.47%.
Rajesh K.N vs Ganesh C.K on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125336287/
4 16. During the cross examination of PW.2, nothing worthwhile is elicited. The petitioner has averred that, at the time of accident he was doing Tailoring and Photograph work and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month. From the evidence of PW.2 it can be seen that the disability being suffered by the petitioner will impact his work. Therefore, the court deems it fit to consider the whole body disability at 20%. 
Monthly income:
17. The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was doing Tailoring work also he is a Photographer and getting income of Rs.20,000/- per month. In this regard he has not produced any documents like Bank statement or any other documents. He has not examined any witness to prove the income of the petitioner. The accident occurred in the year 2022. Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,500/- per month. 
18. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 51 years as could be made out from Exs.P.13, 17 & 19/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card and DL. He was hale and healthy before the accident. Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:- 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Jayadevi Memorial Hospital,
Bangalore, as an inpatient from 07.02.2022 to 28.02.2022, 26.03.2022 to 04.04.2022, discharged with advice to take follow up treatment. In this regard, he has produced Exs.P.9 & 14 Discharge summaries of Smt. Jayadevi Memorial Hospital. Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head. 
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization, medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc., In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.5,84,150/- and Ex.P.16 for a sum of Rs.1,73,869/-. Out of these bills Sl.No.57 at Ex.P.11 and Sl.No.1 at Ex.P.11 one and the same for Rs.4,468/-
it has to deducted. After deduction, the total medical bills comes to Rs.7,53,551/-. 
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent No.2. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head. 
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries. The petitioner has taken treatment for almost 1 month at Smt. Jayadevi Memorial Hospital which can be made out from Exs.P.9 & 14 Discharge summaries. Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Rajesh K.N vs Ganesh C.K on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125336287/
5 Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him. Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.31,000/- under this head. 
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Exs.P.13, 17 & 18/Aadhar Card and DL, the date of birth of the petitioner is 20.06.1971 and the date of accident is 07.02.2022. Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 51 years. As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 11. As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.4,09,200/-. (Rs.15,500/- x 12 x 20% x 11 = Rs.4,09,200/-
). 
 (v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:- 
The Petitioner was aged about 51 years at the time of accident. He has sustained grievous and simple injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 20% functional disability. The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life. Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts. 
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered,
a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head. 
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES: 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted for almost 1 month as an inpatient and discharged with advise. However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment,
conveyance and attendant expenses. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head. 
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
As per the version of the PW.2, the petitioner need further surgeries in the form of Debulking procedure for reduction of flap which may cost approximate Rs.95,000/-
and the petitioner is in need of removal of implants which may cost approximate Rs.70,000/-. In this regard the petitioner or the PW.2 have not produced any estimation letter. Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries, evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head. 
19. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
Rajesh K.N vs Ganesh C.K on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125336287/
6 2. Medical expenses Rs.7,53,551/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.31,000/-
 Loss of Future Income Rs.4,09,200/-
 5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/-
 happiness  6 . Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.30,000/-
 nourishment charges  7. Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.13,43,751/-
If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.13,44,000/- and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner. 
LIABILITY 20. In order to prove their defence the Respondent No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1, who filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination reiterating the objections. He got marked Exs.R.1 & 2 Authorization letter & copy of insurance policy. During his cross-examination he has admitted that the insured vehicle had all the valid documents except permit. But, the same is not mentioned in the charge sheet. The charge sheet is filed against the insured vehicle. The counsel for the petitioner has filed memo with copy of permit when the case was posted for arguments which shows the validity of permit from 09.02.2022 to 08.02.2027. The date of accident is 07.02.2022. 
Therefore, it is clear that as on the date of accident the insured vehicle did not have a permit. As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal No.2253/2018: Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Ins. Co. Ltd., (Supreme Court).
Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that in case of absence of valid permit, the insurance company can be directed to pay and recover. 
Therefore, the respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner and then recover the same from the respondent No.1. 
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.13,44,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. Therefore,
the petition needs to be allowed. Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative. 
21. Issue No.3: 
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:-
Rajesh K.N vs Ganesh C.K on 28 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125336287/
7 ORDER The petition is allowed with cost. 
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,44,000/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs and Forty Four Thousand only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount. 
The Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award. 
The Respondent No.2 is entitled to recover the compensation amount from the Respondent No.1. 
On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any N/S Bank for a period of 3 years and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. Draw decree accordingly. 
(Typed to my dictation directly on the computer by the Stenographer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 28th Day of August 2024). 
(PRAKRITI KALYANPUR) XXIII ASCJ & ACJM, Bangalore.

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Jayadevi Memorial Hospital,

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization, medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.5,84,150/- and Ex.P.16 for a sum of Rs.1,73,869/-.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.

As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for almost 1 month at Smt. Jayadevi Memorial Hospital which can be made out from Exs.P.9 & 14 Discharge summaries.

On perusal of Exs.P.13, 17 & 18/Aadhar Card and DL, the date of birth of the petitioner is 20.06.1971 and the date of accident is 07.02.2022.

The Petitioner was aged about 51 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous and simple injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 20% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered,
a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted for almost 1 month as an inpatient and discharged with advise.

However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment,
conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the version of the PW.2, the petitioner need further surgeries in the form of Debulking procedure for reduction of flap which may cost approximate Rs.95,000/-
and the petitioner is in need of removal of implants which may cost approximate Rs.70,000/-.
In this regard the petitioner or the PW.2 have not produced any estimation letter.
Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries, evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.13,44,000/- and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.

In order to prove their defence the Respondent No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1, who filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination reiterating the objections.
He got marked Exs.R.1 & 2 Authorization letter & copy of insurance policy.
During his cross-examination he has admitted that the insured vehicle had all the valid documents except permit.
But, the same is not mentioned in the charge sheet.
The charge sheet is filed against the insured vehicle.
The counsel for the petitioner has filed memo with copy of permit when the case was posted for arguments which shows the validity of permit from 09.02.2022 to 08.02.2027.
The date of accident is 07.02.2022.
Therefore, it is clear that as on the date of accident the insured vehicle did not have a permit.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal No.2253/2018: Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Ins. Co. Ltd., (Supreme Court).
